title: Meridian daily Codex briefing overlay
description: Apply to the exact collection snapshot. Author every report under docs/EDITORIAL-RULEBOOK.md: plain language, Humanizer editing, sourced perspectives where relevant and an evidence-backed editorial takeaway. Every selected briefing item needs a complete bilingual analysis overlay, an exactly matching summary, and an attention assessment so it appears in the ranked dashboard. Evidence must include the article URL. Publisher translation is imported separately; these cross-array constraints are checked by apply_briefing.py. Validation checks structure and references, not editorial quality or factual truth. Optional analysis.headline and analysis.readerBrief provide English-first reading copy without replacing the factual bilingual analysis; routine imports preserve them when omitted only while summary and the factual analysis core are unchanged. Changed facts require newly authored reading copy. Editorial-only revisions use scripts/apply_editorial.py and $defs/editorialOverlay.

overview.description: Lead with the most useful supported judgment and its practical significance; connect priorities rather than listing headlines. Follow the editorial rulebook and preserve the same claim strength in both languages.

items.description: Select significant developments across the rolling 30-day window, carrying important unread events forward. Do not fill a daily quota with less important new reporting.

articles.description: Complete article-detail overlays. Every selected briefing item requires an exactly matching bilingual summary and an attention assessment. Non-selected extra analyses may omit attention.

zh.description: Chinese prose is required; copying English into zh does not satisfy bilingual coverage.

whyItMatters.description: Labeled editorial assessment: explain the mechanism, who gains or bears costs, and the concrete takeaway. Assess credible competing interpretations by evidence rather than giving each equal weight.

context.description: Brief orientation for a newcomer: explain actors, roles and necessary terms before the detailed development. Avoid unexplained jargon and generic history.

implications.description: Start with the clearest supported editorial judgment in a short paragraph suitable for the briefing preview. Explain how the development affects people or decisions. Add relevant named and sourced commentator or stakeholder perspectives, assess their strongest credible disagreement, and finish with a concrete takeaway. Distinguish Meridian inference from attributed views; no invented voices or mandatory false balance.

uncertainty.description: State the specific missing evidence or credible alternative that could change the assessment. Keep source access limitations precise; do not replace analysis with generic hedging.

watch.description: Name an observable decision, measure or event, and explain what it would strengthen or weaken in the assessment. Use documented dates only.

attention.description: Required semantically for every selected briefing item; optional for non-selected extra analysis overlays.

reverified.description: Set true only after actually rechecking the factual evidence. Identical copied factual analysis keeps its original analyzedAt timestamp unless explicitly reverified; attention.reviewedAt is a separate priority assessment.

eventKey.description: Stable semantic identifier shared by reports about the same event, not an article URL or date.

updateKey.description: Stable identifier for the latest material development. Keep unchanged for duplicate/minor reports; change only with sourced substantive new facts.

readingSection.description: One editorial reading desk for the whole semantic event. Reports sharing eventKey must agree when this field is supplied. Omission preserves an existing assignment and remains accepted for legacy imports; it does not default to a publisher feed category during validation.

zh.description: Chinese prose is required; copying English into zh does not satisfy bilingual coverage.
Chinese prose is required; copying English into zh does not satisfy bilingual coverage.

sectionNoteSummary.description: Concise paired prose: English at most 75 whitespace-delimited words and 650 characters; Chinese at most 180 characters; at most two paragraphs in either language. Aim for 20–40 English words and 40–90 Chinese characters. Word/paragraph limits are also checked by the importer.

summary.description: Latest development, separate from the explanatory background.

articleIds.description: Cite article IDs with complete current bilingual analysis or a retained reviewed snapshot. New reading-desk scopes follow the event readingSection assignment, with mapped primary feed category fallback. Legacy topic scopes retain category/relatedCategories compatibility; all is unrestricted. Membership constraints are checked by apply_briefing.py.

background.description: Previously reviewed background needed to understand the latest development in summary. Supply for newly authored notes; optional for legacy compatibility. Use sourced article.analysis.context, never raw-source speculation. Same bilingual readability limits as summary.

sectionNotes.description: Optional edited notes for the four reading desks: politics, economy, development and industry; all is the cross-desk briefing. Each new-desk note must reference events assigned to that desk, falling back to mapped primary feed category where no assignment exists. Legacy us/world/crisis/sdg scopes and unassigned legacy related-category economy/industry notes remain accepted. Provide background before the latest-development summary. Editing notes or desk assignments does not reverify facts or reset article analyzedAt.

englishFirstHeadline.description: An independently written, concrete reading headline. English is required; Chinese is optional. This editorial copy does not change the publisher title or factual review date.

englishFirstReaderBrief.description: A readable orientation connecting the latest development, necessary background and supported consequence. English at most 220 whitespace-delimited words; at most four paragraphs and 1600 characters per supplied locale. Chinese is optional. Preserve attribution, evidence limits and factual scope; this field does not reverify facts.

editorialOverlay.description: Editorial-only input for apply_editorial.py. Copy the current dashboard generatedAt exactly. Each article must already have complete current analysis or a compatible retained reviewed snapshot. No factual claims, source summaries, evidence, factual timestamps, attention keys or read state are replaced. Briefing generatedAt remains the original factual briefing date.
